thesisQuality.basis: Pure-play automation positioning, installed-base context and post-spin operating evidence support a strong thesis, tempered by separation normalization and uneven segment results.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: 4% organic growth and sharply improved operating/free cash flow are positive, while reported operating margin slipped and segment momentum is mixed.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Current post-spin valuation evidence is limited and capital structure remains in normalization; conservative mixed/unproven band avoids treating uncertainty as favorable.

catalystScore.basis: Automation/autonomous-control rollout and post-spin portfolio simplification are identifiable catalysts, but timing and realized economics remain uncertain.

governancePower.basis: Management completed a major separation and provides recast perimeter disclosure, but leverage, financing charges and dis-synergy uncertainty constrain confidence.

alignment2036.basis: Industrial/building automation and autonomous control address durable productivity, energy, safety and workforce constraints.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Building, process and industrial automation are independent demand engines sharing automation/control capabilities.

bottleneckControl.basis: Installed control-system context and process expertise create switching/integration friction, but no evidence supports exceptional system-critical scarcity.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Diversified automation segments provide multiple demand paths, offset by separation transition and uneven segment momentum.

substitutionResilience.basis: Installed-base integration and process knowledge provide moderate replacement barriers, while competitive technology and cybersecurity validation remain meaningful.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Diversified automation portfolio supports adequate resilience, but current sources do not establish exceptional multi-source redundancy; neutral-strong boundary retained.

pricingPower.basis: Building Automation margin expanded to 27.1% and Industrial Automation margin to 17.2%, supporting pricing/economic capture, while Process Automation margin contracted.

riskEvidence.basis: Separation execution, $34B borrowings, financing-cost normalization, cybersecurity/safety validation and uneven segment momentum are material but not thesis-breaking risks.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Direct SEC post-spin perimeter financials and amended 10-Q materially improve provenance; valuation and long-run separation economics remain less directly evidenced.

scoreRecord.keyRisk: Separation financing/dis-synergies and uneven segment momentum may offset automation growth and distort historical comparability.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Next post-spin quarterly disclosure showing normalized leverage, segment margins, order conversion and cash generation.
